Evaluate ${\int }_{C}\frac{2y}{x}\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the path along the upper-right quarter of the ellipse $9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=36,$ traversed from the point $(2,0)$ to the point $(0,3),$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $2$ and $3,$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=\frac{2y}{x}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =\frac{2\cdot 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\  & =3\operatorname{tan}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(3\operatorname{tan}⁡t)\cdot (3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot \text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =(-9\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))-(-9\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
